title: xchange
headline: xchange
tagline: A mobile currency exchange app for travelers.
summary: A mobile app that gives global travelers quick, reliable access to live exchange rates, so they can convert between currencies, manage travel budgets and make informed decisions abroad.
overview: xchange was created to help international travelers and remote workers track and convert currencies in real time. The app focuses on speed, accuracy and usability, with a simple, clean interface. I designed it while taking the Google UX Design Professional Certificate, following user-centred design principles.
problem: Travelers need reliable, up-to-date exchange rates fast, want to convert between several currencies on the go and keep their travel budget in check, but existing apps are slow, cluttered or hard to navigate.

title: WorldClockr
headline: WorldClockr
tagline: A clean world clock and time-zone converter.
summary: A mobile app that keeps people in sync with time around the world: local time detected automatically, favourite cities at a glance, and a quick converter between any two cities.
overview: WorldClockr is a modern, intuitive mobile app that helps people stay connected with time across the world. It detects the user’s current location, shows the local time, and lets them add favourite cities for quick access. Users can convert time between two cities and manage their list by reordering or deleting any city.
problem: Many people work or communicate across time zones, but most time apps are cluttered, hard to navigate or offer little customisation. Users end up searching “current time in X” or doing mental maths when scheduling meetings or travel.

design: Research into how people track time zones day to day
Review of gaps in existing time apps
User types, needs and pain points
Wireframes and high-fidelity UI
Testing and iteration

process.title: Empathise
process.desc: Understood user needs, problems and behaviours.

process.title: Define
process.desc: Identified the core challenges and opportunities.

process.title: Test
process.desc: Validated ideas and improved them from feedback.

challenges.challenge: Checking the time in another city means searching the web every time.
challenges.solution: Local time detected automatically, with favourite cities listed on the home screen and their offset from you (+7h, −2h) and the day (Yesterday, Today, Tomorrow).

challenges.challenge: Scheduling across time zones takes mental maths.
challenges.solution: A two-city converter that shows the time difference in big type, with a swap button to flip the direction.

challenges.challenge: Existing apps are cluttered and hard to navigate.
challenges.solution: One list, two actions in the header (edit and add), and a dark interface with a single pink accent so the time always stands out.

challenges.challenge: Users want their own list, not a fixed one.
challenges.solution: An edit mode to remove or drag cities into any order, and an add-city sheet with suggested cities and search.
